chunks: And they followed what the devils recited concerning the dominion of Solomon, and Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people sorcery and what was sent down to the two angels in Babylon, Harut and Marut.
And they would not teach anyone until they said, 'We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.'
They learn from them that which separates a man from his wife.
And they cannot harm anyone through it except by the permission of Allah.
And they learn that which harms them and does not benefit them.
And they certainly knew that whoever bought it would have no share in the Hereafter.
And evil is that which they sold themselves with, if they only knew.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Harut and Marut in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse clarifies the doctrine of Ismah (infallibility) of Prophet Solomon, refuting the notion that he practiced magic, while identifying Harut and Marut as either angels or jinn sent as a divine trial (fitnah). The narrative highlights that sorcery's power is contingent upon God's permission, serving as a test of faith rather than an independent force. It underscores the spiritual cost of acquiring this knowledge, where practitioners trade their eternal reward for temporary worldly utility.
